_comment: Authoring anchors for roadmap Unit 5. Core lessons are OLD 2.4-2.8 (NEW 5.1-5.5); Beyond the Exam lessons assigned to Unit 5 are OLD 2.9 and 9.1-9.5. Anchors describe released-FRQ patterns without quoting items.

dok2_anchors.shape: Given paired quantitative data or a scatterplot, assign variables, construct or describe the display, and calculate or interpret correlation in context.
dok2_anchors.why_dok2: The representation and target summary are supplied, so the student follows a standard construction, description, calculation, or interpretation path without adjudicating competing claims.

dok2_anchors.shape: Given a named regression model or slope-inference procedure, calculate and interpret a prediction, residual, coefficient, interval, test statistic, or p-value and check the stated conditions.
dok2_anchors.why_dok2: The model or inference method is already selected; the student executes a known multistep procedure and communicates the requested result.

dok3_anchors.shape: Competing accounts of bivariate data are plausible; coordinate form, direction, strength, unusual observations, correlation, residual behavior, and study design to choose the warranted account and bound its scope or causal meaning.
dok3_anchors.why_dok3: The student must reconcile graphical, numerical, and design evidence that support different parts of the competing accounts and trace the rejected account to a consequence.

dok3_anchors.shape: Several predictions or fitted models compete; choose the one justified by the data range, coefficient meanings, residual diagnostics, transformation, and influence of unusual observations, then explain the practical consequence of the rejected choice.
dok3_anchors.why_dok3: The student aligns model evidence with the prediction purpose, weighs evidence that can point in different directions, and explains the consequence of extrapolation or unstable fit.

dok3_anchors.shape: For a Beyond the Exam slope investigation, choose the question suggested by variation or adjudicate competing interval or test conclusions using residual-based conditions, inferential output, study design, and the population claim.
dok3_anchors.why_dok3: No isolated calculation settles the investigation; the student must connect the question, diagnostic, inferential, and design evidence and explain how an unsupported conclusion would mislead a reader.

not_dok3: A longer calculation of correlation, a regression line, a prediction, a residual, or a slope-inference statistic after the model or method has been selected.
A complete direction-form-strength-unusual-features description that never asks the student to adjudicate a competing description or consequence.
An interpretation prompt that supplies the correct coefficient, interval, p-value, or conclusion and asks the student to restate it in context.
Lettered parts that separately graph, calculate, check conditions, and describe but never require a judgment about a model, claim, prediction, inference, or scope.
Calling a large absolute correlation proof of linear form or causation, or treating a slope interval or p-value as decisive without diagnostics and study design.
